- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mean to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, reduce forecasted mean by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.  
- If forecasted price exceeds true outcome by >10% in the first 5–7 days, apply a “lag correction” — reduce subsequent days’ forecast by 1–3% to reflect delayed market reaction.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and forecast is volatile, smooth the curve by averaging adjacent forecast values to avoid noise-driven overfitting.
